answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a bond locked for a fixed period, with each bond capped per verified participant. A challenge period lets peers expose duplicate identities; proven duplicates forfeit their bonds to challengers, while honest agents recover funds after the lock expires. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must immobilize capital across many identities and risks losing it. A comet of new accounts, a whisper network, or a trellis of referrals cannot bypass the bond and duplicate checks.
